claim.why_it_matters: A heading at the wrong level (or none) misplaces the clause in the outline that page_workunit, citation and section lookups read, so the clause is attributed to the wrong parent or not found as a section.
claim.note: Heading at the wrong level: the transcription's convention is one '#' per numbering component (7. is '#', 7.1 '##', 6.4.1 '###', 6.4.2.1 '####', 6.4.2.1.1 '#####'); should be '####'.

verdict.reasoning: Printed page IV-39 (PDF p185) shows the heading '6.4.2.4 Delimited Scope Statements' and the markdown carries the same text, so nothing is missing; the defect is the level. The number has four components, and in this same Procedure Division section the transcription gives 6.4.2 '###' and 6.4.2.1 '####' (specs/ANSI_COBOL_1985.md lines 7623, 7629), yet 6.4.2.4 is '###' (line 7738). At '###' it reads in the outline as a sibling of 6.4.2 rather than its child, which misplaces the clause for heading-based section lookup. Quotes of both sources are accurate.
verdict.corrected_description: The heading is present with the correct text but at the wrong level: '### 6.4.2.4 Delimited Scope Statements' should be '#### ...' (four-component number, child of 6.4.2 which is '###'). The same off-by-one level affects its siblings in this section, 6.4.2.2 and 6.4.2.3 (lines 7683, 7701, both '###') and their subclauses (6.4.2.2.x, 6.4.2.3.x at '####'); and 6.4.3 Scope of Statements at line 7748 is '##' instead of '###'.
